message.content:
**Triangulation Metrics – A Quick Overview** | What it measures | Why it matters | Typical use‑cases | |------------------|---------------|-------------------| | **Accuracy & precision of position estimates** obtained through *geometric triangulation* (e.g., GPS, Wi‑Fi, BLE). | Helps you know how close your computed location is to reality and how repeatable it is over time. | Indoor positioning systems, autonomous navigation, asset tracking. | | **Consistency between independent measurement sets** (different devices, different algorithms). | Detects systematic biases or errors that only show up when comparing two “views” of the same event. | Multi‑sensor fusion validation, quality control pipelines. | | **Coverage / completeness** of triangulation attempts within a defined window (last X days). | Gives insight into operational reliability—how often do you actually get usable triangulations versus failures? | Service level monitoring, capacity planning. | ### How It’s Calculated 1. **Position Error** \[ e_i = \lVert\mathbf{p}_i^{(est)} - \mathbf{p}^{(true)}_i\rVert \] where \( \mathbf{p}_i^{(est)} \) comes from the triangulation algorithm and \( \mathbf{p}^{(true)}_i \) is ground truth (from high‑accuracy reference). 2. **Statistical Summary** • Mean error (bias) \( \bar{e}\ )
• Root‑mean‑square error (RMSE) \( \sqrt{\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^N e_i^2 } \)
• Standard deviation (precision) 3. **Cross‑Method Agreement** For each timestamp compare two independently derived points: \[ d_{\text{cross}} = \lVert \mathbf{p}_{A,i}^{(est)}-\mathbf{p}_{B,i}^{(est)} \rVert \] 4. **Success Rate** \[ R_{\text{succ}}=\frac{\text{Number of successful triangulations}}{\text{Total trials}} \] These numbers feed directly into dashboards, alerts, and automated decision logic—for example, flagging a branch whose success rate has dropped below 95% or automatically re‑calibrating an indoor map when RMSE spikes beyond a threshold. --- #### Bottom Line “Triangulation metrics” give you a quantitative handle on **where**, **when**, and **why** your triangulation system works well—or fails—to help maintain service quality, guide engineering improvements, and satisfy regulatory or SLA requirements.
